chapter: Paul Mares and the Rhythm Kings
title: Paul's barbecue place and jam sessions in Chicago
summary: Mares remembers the Monday-night jam sessions at Paul's barbecue place with the Bobcats, Baby Dodds and Lee Collins; Russell recalls visiting in 1938.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I heard him play one night up there when he had the barbecue on Monday nights seems that everybody has these sessions Monday nights on his barbecue place up on State Street did you ever see that

oh yeah I was there in fact in 36 I believe it was I was up there when Paul used to have he had the P&M then at that time that's the one where I went well he had all the jam sessions of course the Bobcats were there Eddie Miller Bob Zerkey and he used to have Baby Dodds because Baby Dodds was his favorite drummer and he used to send for Lee Collins all the time and Warren Smith and Georgie and all of them all the top jazz men in that territory around Chicago would always come out to Paul's and they'd all jam and have some of them real real good old New Orleans jam sessions Paul never gave it up he always liked it and Paul was a good jazz man that is from all around from trying to keep it going and playing it and what you call sleeping it eating it and everything else Paul was a real jazz man all the way around Bill he loved it and he's never knocked anybody he's always tried to help and tried to do the right thing

he was a very wonderful fellow I only knew him a couple of nights you might say we were working on the book Jazzman I went there to interview him in 1938 I remember one Monday session maybe more than one at that time he didn't seem to be playing regularly I mean he had this little restaurant so he must have given up music professionally
he wouldn't hold a lip and like I say he'd have Lee Collins there and Mac Portland you know when
